# Other useful tidbits

## Notes on shared software

### Using GitHub

Git is a version control system that can be used to synchronize files between the web and local directories. [GitHub](https://github.com/) is a user-friendly website which hosts files and depends on Git.

### Shared code locations

Most of the R packages and code used in NWFSC assessments are listed in the README at <https://github.com/pfmc-assessments>. Other sources not included in this github organization include [Stock Synthesis](https://github.com/nmfs-stock-synthesis/stock-synthesis) and associated packages including [{r4ss}](https://github.com/r4ss/r4ss/) and [{ss3diags}](https://github.com/jabbamodel/ss3diags) (not yet used for PFMC assessments).

In addition, [NMFS OpenSci](https://github.com/orgs/nmfs-opensci/repositories) has a number of NMFS templates for websites, quarto, Rmd docs, and presentations.

We build assessment reports as reproducible quarto documents using the automatic stock assessment report or [{asar}](https://github.com/nmfs-ost/asar) package which is maintained by the NMFS Office of Science and Technology.

## Shared computing resources

In most cases, stock assessment models can be built and explored locally on your assigned laptop. However, occasionally you need additional computing power. This is less common for stock assessments for management and more common for research purposes when you might be running a lot of simulations. PEP has two computers that are available for group use. Contact Owen to gain access.

-   Prometheus:

    -   NWCDW04327574

    -   Located in 209S (i.e., Megsie's office)

    -   Set up as a server so multiple users can utilize the resource at once. Intel Xenon 2.5 GHz processor, 128 GB RAM, 24 cores/48 threads, 1.86 TB storage (D drive)

-   Leafcutter:

    -   NWCDW04327533

    -   Located in 224S (i.e., debrief room / meeting room)

    -   Single-user computer. Intel Xenon 3.00 GHz processor, 64 GB RAM (comparable to laptops), 18 cores/36 threads, 1.84 TB storage

Note that when you parallelize processes over many cores, your RAM needs increase substantially. The process you are trying to replicate will slow down if you become RAM-limited.
